projects.title: Bartop arcade (Batocera)
projects.summary: Turn a working laptop into a one-player bartop with a printed or wood cabinet, USB controls, and Batocera on a USB stick or internal drive.
parts: Working laptop (14–17" class fits most docks; confirm your design)
USB arcade joystick + buttons kit (one player)
USB flash drive (16 GB+) for Batocera, or install Batocera to internal storage
3D-printed dock/cabinet OR wood/MDF panels from published plans
Stock laptop AC adapter
Optional: external speakers if the laptop speakers face the wrong way
steps: Decide dock vs gut: dock keeps the laptop intact (easier, reversible); gutting transplants the panel and board into a custom case (harder, better fit).
Download Batocera from batocera.org and write it to USB (or install to disk).
Boot once on a desk, update Batocera, set video mode to the laptop’s native resolution, and test a controller.
Print or cut the cabinet. InventorMike’s Laptop Arcade Dock fits 14–17" laptops; wood plans (WeeCade, Holbrook, Pete Clarke) need measuring your lid thickness and bezel.
Mount the control panel, route USB to the laptop, and secure the chassis so vents stay clear.
Cable-manage the AC adapter; leave a service hatch so you can remove the battery later.
safety: Remove or disconnect the Li-ion battery before drilling, sawing, or soldering near the chassis.
Never puncture, crush, or short a laptop battery — swollen packs go to proper e-waste recycling.
Keep intake/exhaust vents unobstructed; bartops can cook a Core 2 Duo or U-series CPU.
Use the original wattage (or higher, Dell-compatible) AC adapter only.

projects.title: Digital photo frame / stand
projects.summary: Run a full-screen slideshow or Immich/Jellyfin client on an old laptop propped as a frame — tent mode on 2-in-1s is ideal.
parts: Laptop with a decent screen
Lightweight OS or kiosk browser (Linux + feh/mpv, or a digital-signage image)
Photo source (local folder, NAS share, Immich, etc.)
Stand, 3D-printed easel, or use 2-in-1 tent/stand mode
AC adapter (leave battery removed for always-on duty if safe for your model)
steps: Clean install a lightweight OS or configure the existing OS for auto-login + fullscreen slideshow.
Point the slideshow at your photo library (local sync or network).
Disable sleep, dimming, and noisy fans where possible; set a conservative brightness.
Build or print a stand that tips the screen back 10–20°, or use the 5579’s hinge modes.
Hide cables; label the power brick wattage on the frame back.
safety: Always-on frames: remove the battery if the vendor supports AC-only operation, or leave it installed but cool and monitored — heat + aging Li-ion is the risk.
Do not block vents behind a wall mount.
Use a surge-protected outlet for unattended devices.

projects.title: Car headrest monitor
projects.summary: Harvest a laptop LCD (or use a thin 2-in-1) as a rear-seat display with an HDMI/eDP controller board and a headrest mount.
parts: Laptop LCD panel with known interface (LVDS 30/40-pin or eDP)
Matching LCD controller board (HDMI/VGA in) + inverter if CCFL
12 V → board voltage DC-DC (verify board input, often 12 V)
Headrest mount or custom 3D-printed/wood bracket for your seat posts
Automotive fuse tap or accessory power with proper fusing
Optional: USB media player or phone HDMI adapter as the source
steps: Photograph and read the panel sticker (model, resolution, connector) before ordering a controller.
Bench-test panel + controller + power supply on a desk until you get a stable image.
Design a shallow enclosure; keep high-voltage CCFL inverter leads insulated.
Mount to the headrest; strain-relief every cable; fuse the 12 V feed close to the source.
Route cables so airbags, seat travel, and passengers stay clear.
safety: Vehicle electrical work: disconnect the car battery before tapping power; fuse every new circuit.
CCFL inverters produce high voltage — treat as hazardous even when powered down until discharged.
Laptop Li-ion packs do not belong loose in a car cabin; recycle them — power the display from vehicle 12 V via the controller board only.
Never obstruct airbags or headrest safety function; if unsure, use a commercial headrest monitor instead.

projects.title: Kiosk / dashboard
projects.summary: Lock a laptop into a single-purpose dashboard: home status, Immich album, pinball card display, or a simple web kiosk.
parts: Laptop with working Wi-Fi or Ethernet
Kiosk browser / Electron / Chromium --kiosk, or a dedicated dashboard OS
Wall bracket, VESA adapter (if harvesting a panel), or a printed stand
AC adapter on a switched outlet or smart plug
steps: Pick the URL or local app the kiosk should always show.
Configure auto-login, disable updates that steal the screen, and set Chromium/Firefox kiosk flags or a Weston/Cage session.
Mount the machine; leave USB accessible for recovery keyboards.
Document the login and recovery steps on a card taped inside the stand.
safety: Unattended kiosks: remove or secure the battery, protect against theft, and use a GFCI/surge outlet.
Do not leave passwords on a sticky note facing the public — use a local kiosk account with minimal privileges.
